You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:

content.text:
Based on the preoperative supine chest radiograph (Figure 4) of the 92-year-old patient, which of the following findings is most indicative of pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis, and how does it support this diagnosis over other potential conditions?
A. Bilateral, diffuse, ill-defined calcifications with relative sparing of the upper left lobe, consistent with the pattern of PAM.
B. Presence of linear calcifications along the pleural surfaces, suggesting tuberculosis.
C. Bilateral, homogeneously dense opacities indicating diffuse alveolar septal amyloidosis.
D. Confluent nodular opacities predominantly in the upper lobes, typical of sarcoidosis.
E. Diffuse reticular pattern with calcified lymph nodes, indicative of coal workers' pneumoconiosis.
F. Upper lobe cavitation with surrounding calcifications, suggestive of post-primary tuberculosis.
